title: Marcos hails ‘successful’ Philippines chairship of ASEAN
summary: President Marcos turned over the chairship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations to Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and described the Philippines’ hosting of the bi-annual…

blocks.text: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. hands over the ceremonial wooden gavel to Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, marking the transfer of the ASEAN chairmanship on November 17, 2026.

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos turned over the chairship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations to Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and described the Philippines’ hosting of the bi-annual meeting of the 11-member regional bloc as “successful.”
Marcos also called on leaders to ensure that ASEAN’s progress would continue to be felt by its people.
In his speech during the closing ceremony, Marcos said the Philippines’ chairship would be remembered not only for what leaders decided upon, “but for what ASEAN is now better able to do.”

“The ASEAN takes prominence in summits such as these, but it must be brought to life every day across our region by ministers, by officials, negotiators and experts, businesses and civil society, young people, communities and by the countless people who work quietly behind the scenes to give meaning to our ambitions and to make our work of real consequence,” he said.

“I am so happy that we were able to bring that team together, and that they worked so well together that we were in the end able to do what we have to achieve and what we have succeeded to do in this ASEAN. So I think it is a success,” Marcos said at a press conference at the International Media Center.
The President cited the important outcomes of the three-day summit, including the signing of the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement.
Marcos expressed support for Singapore’s ASEAN’s chairship next year.
He is confident that Singapore would lead “with a clarity of purpose, steadiness and commitment to regional cooperation for which it is known and for which these times demand.”
“The most important work of ASEAN cannot belong to one chair alone. Progress endures when each chair builds on what came before and leaves stronger foundations for what comes next,” he said.

For his part, Wong said 2026 has been a challenging year for the region and the world, but “ASEAN has remained united and continued to move forward with ambition and purpose” under the leadership of the Philippines.
Aside from the leaders from ASEAN and dialogue partners, also present at the closing were former president and now Pampanga Rep. Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo and other government officials.

Among those who performed during the closing ceremony at the Philippine International Convention Center in Pasay City were singer-songwriter Gary Valenciano and SB19, who performed “Together in Motion,” the official theme song of the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits.
SB19 is a tourism ambassador for the Philippines.
Leaders and guests cheered when Timor-Leste Prime Minister Kay Rala Xanana Gusmao danced with the performers.
Timor Leste will chair the ASEAN in 2029.
